Choosing your Ather

The best Ather for a long daily commute

A growing number of our customers ride 50 km or more every day — Chengalpattu to Guindy, Siruseri to Anna Nagar, Chidambaram to Neyveli. An Ather handles that comfortably, but the model, the battery and the charging plan all need to be right.

Updated 12 November 2026 · 2 min read · Pillai Auto, authorised Ather dealer

The best Ather for a long daily commute

On this page

  1. Choose the 3.5 kWh battery
  2. Which model for which commute
  3. Plan your charging around the day
  4. Ride efficiently without riding slowly

Choose the 3.5 kWh battery

For 50 km and over, we nearly always recommend the 3.5 kWh pack. Its TrueRange of about 125–130 km means a 60 km round trip uses less than half the battery, leaving a comfortable margin for traffic, detours and Sport mode. On the 450X, 450 Apex and Rizta Z it also unlocks fast charging at up to 30 km in ten minutes.

Which model for which commute

CommuteOur pickWhy
Fast highway stretches (GST Road, OMR)450X or 450 Apex90–100 km/h, dual discs, Infinite Cruise
Long commute with a pillionRizta ZComfortable seat, 3.5 kWh option, SkidControl
Long but slow, rough roadsKonarc S 3.5 kWh14-inch wheel, long-travel suspension

Plan your charging around the day

  • Charge at home every night to about 80–90%. Daily top-ups are kinder to the battery than running it low.
  • Find one fast charger on your route in the Ather app before you need it. Ten minutes while you buy tea is a useful safety net.
  • Ask about charging at work. Many OMR offices allow it — a portable charger in the boot doubles your daily range.

Ride efficiently without riding slowly

SmartEco mode adjusts power to how you ride and noticeably stretches range on long trips. Holding a steady 50–60 km/h uses far less energy than repeatedly accelerating hard to 80. On the 450X and Apex, Infinite Cruise's City Cruise keeps your speed steady without holding the throttle. See our range tips.

Questions we get asked

Yes. With the 3.5 kWh battery, Ather's real-world TrueRange estimate is about 125–130 km, so a 100 km day is possible on one charge with sensible riding, or comfortably with a short fast-charge stop.

On rough roads at moderate speeds, yes — especially the 3.5 kWh variant. If your commute includes long stretches above 60 km/h, a 450 is more relaxed.

More cycles do age a battery over time, which is why the extended battery warranty (up to 10 years or 1,00,000 km) is worth considering for high-mileage riders.
